To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Receptor-receptor interactions are the main integrative mechanism taking part in the plasma membrane and the check-point concept is an important tool for drug development”.

1) receptor-receptor interactions play a major role in brain function; 2) receptor mosaics are the molecular basis of receptor-receptor interactions; 3) the disaggregation theory for receptor–G-protein interactions is a consequence of receptor-receptor interaction and 4) allosteric modulators can be designed to target specific amino acids along the amino acid chains connecting the allosteric and the orthosteric site of a receptor.
the receptor-receptor interactions, in particular, the A2A;A1 and A2A;5HT2A receptor interactions are involved in brain integration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the integrative function of the brain and the possibility to modulate these mechanisms by means of allosteric ligands.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of brain integrative functions at plasma membrane level.
the study of receptor-receptor interactions and their role in the integration of the information flow at the plasma membrane level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new concept of receptor–receptor interactions is a promising approach for understanding the molecular mechanisms of the brain integration and for the development of new therapeutic strategies in the field of neurology.

receptor mosaics are a novel integrative mechanism that may be involved in the modulation of receptor activity and, consequently, in the modulation of the molecular networks associated to the plasma membrane.
receptor-receptor interactions, in addition to their importance for receptor function, are also important for the organization of the plasma membrane and its role as an integrative unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
receptor-receptor interactions may be an important mechanism for the brain integration.
the concept of receptor-receptor interactions and the associated molecular networks is a promising new approach to the understanding of brain integration and drug action.
the receptor mosaics are the basic structural and functional units in the plasma membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
receptor-receptor interactions are a novel mechanism of brain integration, which may have important implications in pharmacology.

the receptor mosaic concept is not a simple model of receptor clustering, but rather a complex model that can explain many phenomena in the cell, such as receptor desensitization, receptor internalization and recycling, and allosterism.

receptor-receptor interactions are an important mechanism of brain integration, that they are not restricted to GPCR-GPCR interactions but also include other receptors, and that they may be involved in the control of the allosteric sites of the receptor.
